The distinction is clinically meaningful given the case turns on whether end-organ involvement is present. The standalone bow-tie does not contain this term and is unaffected.

reasoning: The standalone bow-tie was answerable to the canonical key from the stem, prompts, and token pools alone, and the blind Stage 2 record demonstrates this empirically: it selected C1, A1+A2, P2+P3 with no sibling material in context and reached blindExactMatch. Every keyed token traces to text present in the standalone stem — C1 to 'the 1800 monitoring check was missed after an incomplete, dismissive handoff' and 'She has just discovered that the amlodipine dose was increased today'; A1 to the stated call parameter 'a call if SBP > 180' against the stated 'BP is 186/102 with a headache'; P2 to the named handoff defect plus the uncommunicated medication change; P3 to 'BP monitoring q4h x 24 hours' plus the stated omission. A2 is the only keyed token resting on a general-knowledge link rather than direct stem text, and the link (private, behavior-specific, patient-impact-framed, policy-documented feedback for observed unprofessional conduct) is standard professional practice, not a case-specific fact. Every non-keyed token was eliminable without sibling data: C2, C3, A3, and A4 are contradicted by the stem or by professional standards, P4 has no premise of any kind, and P1 fails on relevance to the selected condition independent of whether laboratory values exist. Inspecting the sibling now confirms rather than supplies: all ten missing client facts from the standalone-unblinding record are either corroborated by the case study or absent from it as well, and none of them is load-bearing for any keyed selection. The sibling in fact strengthens the P1 call — the case study supplies exactly the renal data whose absence the blind record noted (CKD stage 3b, creatinine 1.6, eGFR 34), and its own q6 rationale still rejects the creatinine trend because 'it does not measure whether the handoff failure was resolved,' which matches the blind record's judgment that P1 fails on relevance rather than on missing facts. The bow-tie is a faithful condensation of sibling q3 (condition), q4/q5 (actions), and q6 (parameters), with keyed tokens that are near-verbatim reuses of the case study's own keyed options; no bow-tie token depends on a fact that lives only in the exhibits or stages. Because there is no hidden-case dependency, no unsupported keyed-token premise, no underdetermination, and no key or logic defect, and because I do not disagree with the canonical key, precedence resolves to PASS_STANDALONE. The collateral items recorded below — the ambiguous 'She' antecedent and unnamed actor role in the standalone stem, the absent 'Behavior-focused feedback' glossary entry, and two sibling-only translation/clinical wording issues — are advisory and did not affect rankability.

scopeCollateral.observation: The standalone stem's second sentence begins 'She has just discovered that the amlodipine dose was increased today.' The antecedent of 'She' is ambiguous between Priya (the immediately preceding subject) and the unnamed reader/charge nurse who receives Priya's report. The sibling disambiguates — Priya finds the 1400 hospitalist note and Marcus verifies the threshold — but the standalone leaves it open. The ambiguity is inert for selection because both readings yield the same keyed set, but it is a clarity defect.

The sibling supplies the missing frame (Marcus Chen, charge nurse). This was flagged at LOW impact in the blind record and did not prevent correct selection, since no pool action is available to a non-supervisory nurse that would compete with A2.

The sibling's q5 makes the pedagogical point explicit — the charge nurse should ensure the call happens and support Priya rather than take over — but the standalone bow-tie gives no cue that delegation-versus-takeover is at issue. scopeCollateral.observation: The standalone item compresses three sibling NGN skills (prioritize_hypotheses, generate_solutions, evaluate_outcomes) into one bow-tie. The compression is clean and the keyed content is preserved, but the bow-tie inherits the sibling's Stage 2/Stage 3 timeline in a single stem, which is why the actor and role details thin out. This is a structural observation about the derivation, not a defect in the standalone item as presented.

The standalone item is correctly self-contained on de-identification: no sibling proper nouns (Renee Talbot, Marcus Chen, room 312) leak into the tokens or rationales, and no token references an exhibit, stage, or laboratory value that exists only in the case study.

secondaryFlags: Blind Stage 2 reproduced the canonical key exactly with no sibling material in context, which is direct evidence of standalone answerability rather than an inference about it.

All five keyed bow-tie tokens are near-verbatim condensations of keyed options in the sibling questions (C1 from q3 option B, A1 from q4 option A / q5 option A, A2 from q4 option B, P2 from q6 option C, P3 from q6 option D); the bow-tie is a faithful compression of q3+q4+q6 with no added dependency.

All six non-keyed bow-tie tokens likewise mirror sibling distractors with matching rationales (A3 from q3 option A / q5 option B, A4 from q4 option F, C3 from q3 option C, P1 from q6 option F, P4 from q6 option E); only C2 ('routine interpersonal friction') has no direct sibling analog, though sibling q2 row r5 encodes the same 'not incivility by itself' concept.

The sibling caps the bow-tie's action set: sibling q4 keys four actions (A/B/C/D), of which the bow-tie retains only two. The dropped ones — coaching Priya, and completing the safety report plus manager notification — are legitimately absent from the bow-tie action pool but their content resurfaces inside A2 ('policy-based documentation') and P3 ('absence of further care omissions'), so no keyed content is lost.

The Stage 1 free-generation divergence (clinical 'hypertensive urgency' vs. keyed 'communication breakdown') is a designed feature of the pool framing, not an item defect; sibling q3 confirms the intended systems reading and its rationale for option A concedes that 'the conflict is an upstream cause' while the safety gap is the priority.

The bow-tie's condition pool is exhaustively non-clinical, so a test-taker who reasons clinically first (as the Stage 1 record did) is not penalized at selection time; the pool itself performs the reframing.
No keyed token requires knowledge of Mrs. Vega's CKD, HFpEF, diabetes, telemetry, or laboratory status, all of which are sibling-exclusive.
